Definition: or μή τις from G3361 and G5100; whether any:--any (sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence).
BiblicalUsage: The disciples ask whether any man has brought Jesus something to eat, and whether any of the rulers have believed on Him, and Jesus asks the children whether they have any meat. The word is two words in the Greek, whether any, joined into one question, and it stands where the answer is hoped for but not certain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe these three questions show how the word works: the disciples wonder, the rulers are weighed, and the children answer no, and in each case the question itself does the work.
